en: Liquid water is about nine percent denser than solid ice, which is why ice cubes float in a glass of water.
Diamond is the hardest natural material on Earth, scoring a perfect ten on the Mohs hardness scale, while graphite scores only one.
Average ocean water contains about thirty-five grams of dissolved salt per liter, making it a homogeneous mixture called a solution.
When liquid water boils into steam, it expands roughly one thousand seven hundred times in volume to become a gas.
Gold is highly malleable, meaning one single ounce of the metal can be hammered into a thin sheet covering nine square meters.
Earth's atmosphere is a mixture of gases containing roughly seventy-eight percent nitrogen and twenty-one percent oxygen by volume.
A single drop of water contains over one sextillion water molecules, showing how tiny the particles of liquid matter are.
Homogenized milk is a colloid where tiny fat droplets measuring about one micrometer across are evenly dispersed in liquid water.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, requiring a massive three thousand four hundred degrees Celsius to become liquid.
Sound waves travel about four times faster in liquid water than in air, and roughly seventeen times faster in solid steel.
Burning wood is a chemical change where over ninety-nine percent of the solid wood turns into invisible carbon dioxide and water vapor.
Mercury is the only metal that remains liquid at standard room temperature, melting at a low negative thirty-nine degrees Celsius.
